summary: Iteration 3 testing complete. All new backend endpoints pass (cost-constants GET/PUT, library/skus, library/export) and the updated dashboard summary + P&L now correctly include operational_eur and production_shipping_eur with math validated row-by-row. Frontend E2E confirms: language toggle (EN default active dark bg, FR persists to localStorage and across navigation, sidebar translates to French — 'Bibliothèque', 'Compte de résultat'); Library page with searchable+sortable+exportable table; Products Excel-like filters (text 'contains' on sku, numeric min/max on margin_pct, icon turns blue when active, clear-all-filters resets, sort headers work); Settings cost-constants card (op-cost-input, prod-shipping-{mk} inputs, save-constants-button saves with toast 'saved'); P&L renders new rows '− Operational Cost' and '− Production Shipping' with per-marketplace values matching units × constant exactly (Amazon Vendor 5,701u × €0.30 = €1,710.30; Leroy Merlin 1,857u × €0.40 = €742.80; BOL.COM 81u × €0.50 = €40.50). 10/10 new pytest tests pass.

minor.issue: Field name collision: column is called 'production_shipping_cost' but it is sourced from the per-SKU legacy cost file (c['shipping_cost']), NOT from production_shipping_by_marketplace settings. P&L uses the same label for a different concept (per-marketplace × units). May confuse users — consider renaming the Library column to 'SKU Shipping Cost' or clarifying in UI.

issues: Many SKUs show Operational Cost €0.50 and Production Shipping €8.44/€14.44 inherited from legacy cost rows. 'Units Sold' column shows 0 for the top rows because they came from cost file but never appeared in orders — consider hiding zero-units rows or sorting by units desc by default (currently sort defaults to units desc but ties are alphabetical, so 0-unit cost-only SKUs appear first because there are 4,000+ of them).
Amazon Vendor still shows COGS €0.00 (Amazon ASIN SKUs have no cost rows). Carried from iteration 2 — not a new regression.

action_items: (Optional) Rename Library column 'Production Shipping' to clarify it is SKU-level shipping from cost file, distinct from per-marketplace constant used in P&L.
(Carry-over from iter 2) Amazon Vendor still has €0 COGS because Amazon ASIN SKUs have no matching cost rows — needs a SKU mapping layer.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1349 lines — should be split into routers (auth, uploads, dashboard, library, costs) and parsers module.
/api/cost-constants PUT has no role check (any authenticated user can edit costs that affect all reports). Add admin-only guard.
/api/library/skus loads ALL orders aggregated + ALL costs into RAM each request (no pagination on aggregation, only on output). Acceptable at 5k SKUs but will not scale.
/api/library/export internally calls library_skus(limit=20000) — full re-computation on every CSV download. Consider caching the SKU list (TTL 60s) since constants rarely change.
Library 'production_shipping_cost' field name overlaps semantically with P&L 'production_shipping_eur' but represents a different number. Either rename in API or document.
Frontend P&L row labels 'Operational Cost' and 'Production Shipping' are hard-coded in English — should also be translated via the i18n DICT for consistency with the FR toggle.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (language toggle, Library, Products filters, Settings, P&L all verified)

seed_data_creation: PUT /api/cost-constants was used during tests to set op=0.5 and {Amazon Vendor:0.3, Leroy Merlin:0.4, BOL.COM:0.5}. Test resets values via PUT after each run.

Run with: cd /app/backend/tests && pytest -v. Current cost constants in DB: op=0.5, mk={Amazon Vendor:0.3, Leroy Merlin:0.4, BOL.COM:0.5}.
